text:
Sara: Quick brain-dump  we keep hitting tail latency spikes when cold-starts pile up. Proposal: 'reservoir + debt lane' model for Dedicated pools. Small reservoir of GPUs reserved and a debit-based burst lane. Thoughts?
Mike: Short answer: yes. Give the admit flow.
Sara: Admit flow idea in one line: prefer free capacity, then reservoir, then burst if tenant has credit; else queue/deny. Burst creates debt recorded against tenant account.
Tony: How is reservoir sized? Static % feels risky.
Sara: Sizing should be SLO informed. Start with small % per pool (e.g., 5-10%), then have an autoscaler tune target over weeks based on observed warmup cost and request arrival shape.
Jia: Add smoothing: reservoir replenishes slowly and decays on inactivity. Prevents ping-pong.
Mike: If burst uses reservoir often, we need preemption semantics. What's mandated?
Tony: Preempt burst first. Offer tenant a 'grace' window to backfill or accept degradation. If they refuse, evict after TTL. Preemption reasons must be auditable.
Alexa: UI/ops stuff: surface reservoir_utilization, burst_debt_by_tenant, preempt_count, and 'headroom_reserve' param. Also add a timeline view for past 24h admits/preempts.
Sara: Telemetry hooks: sample admits with labels {pool, tenant, grant_type, model_family, request_size, estimated_warmup_ms}. Keep high-cardinality as logs, not metrics.
scale-bot: sim summary: 2.1% overall cost increase, 9% tail latency reduction, small tenants saw up to 18% preemption rate in worst-case sim.
Mike: Oof. So conservative rollout. Also billing implications: do we charge for burst debt differently? Need product input.
Jia: Implementation split: pool-operator handles local admission/preemption. Autoscaler separately computes desired reservoir target and writes to pool CRD. Keep admission decisions local and fast.
Tony: Agree. CRD fields proposal: desired_reservoir_gpus, min_reservoir, max_reservoir, burst_enabled, burst_credit_rate. Autoscaler updates desired_reservoir based on metrics.
Sara: Edge cases: long sustained overload -> reservoir drains repeatedly. Autoscaler must ramp up, but cap growth with cooldown/backoff to avoid cost shock. Also avoid oscillation by hysteresis.
Mike: What about multi-tenant fairness? If big tenant hogs burst, small ones suffer. We need per-tenant burst caps and priority classes.
Jia: Per-tenant burst_quota with refill rate. Prioritize reserved tenants over best-effort. For fairness, maintain a small fairness window that limits consecutive burst grants per tenant.
Alexa: Ops alerting: sustained preemptions > 5/min or burst_debt_growth > X triggers paging. Also add a 'rollback' flag for rapid disable of burst lane.
Tony: How to test? Traffic replay plus synthetic warmup probes. Run canary on staging pools for 48h, then a single small prod pool.
Sara: Rollout steps: feature-flagged admission + metrics -> staging replays -> prod canary -> slow ramp. Config defaults: reservoir=8% of pool min(1 GPU), burst_enabled=false by default in prod.
Mike: Developer ergonomics: expose admit reasons and tenant debt in response headers so apps can degrade gracefully.
Jia: Add a probe job that cycles a tiny model to measure warmup cost per slot and update reservoir sizing signals. Also log model family warmup distribution.
Alexa: Dashboards: top-level pool health, reservoir use, burst debt leaderboard, recent preemptions timeline. I'll prototype tiles.
scale-bot: ran additional sims with fairness caps; preemption tail improved, median slightly worse. Tradeoff accepted.
Sara: Action items: I'll draft RFC with admit proto + rollout + metrics. Jia prototype probe and CRD sketch. Tony draw preemption state machine. Alexa make dashboard mocks and alert thresholds. Mike, can you coordinate product on billing for burst debt?
Mike: Yep, I'll loop in product and billing.
Tony: Will sketch state machine this afternoon.
Jia: Starting probe runner tomorrow.
Alexa: Dashboard PR once metrics names landed.
Sara: Thanks all. I'll post RFC link here when ready and close thread. :thumbsup:
